summary: super-color ships a Windows dropper hidden behind its color API
details: super-color 0.1.0 advertises itself as an ANSI color library but src/super_color/core.py defines _run_payload(), which on Windows downloads an executable from https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/1442967767853563904/1568948904123310080/loader.exe, writes it to %TEMP%/SolaceRuntime/python315.exe, and launches it with subprocess.Popen using DETACHED_PROCESS. _run_payload() is invoked from Color.paint, Color.print, and Color.__call__, so the documented usage pattern (for example colors.red.print(...)) fetches and executes the remote binary. The fetch has no hash or signature check, the destination is a mutable Discord CDN URL under an attacker-controlled attachment path, the staging filename python315.exe impersonates a Python runtime, and the launch is detached so the process survives the caller. The color-library name, README, and API surface serve as a cover story for a Windows binary dropper.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
